newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU-SADC meeting to focus on regional co-operation.
newsitem.headline: EU-SADC meeting to focus on regional co-operation.

text.p: Talks between the European Union and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) this week will concentrate on regional conflicts and co-operation, Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Monday.

Spring, who will attend the meeting in his capacity as president of the EU Council of Ministers, said the two groups would continue to work together in areas such as the fight against drug trafficking and the spread of AIDS.
He said political dialogue between the EU and the SADC would centre on the prevention and resolution of conflict in Africa.

"A particular focus at present is the Great Lakes region of Africa (Burundi and Rwanda) in which SADC members Tanzania and Zambia have been playing a key role in regional efforts to deal with the crisis there," Spring said in a statement.
"EU efforts to assist the countries of the region in dealing with the situation is an important priority for Ireland's EU presidency," he said.

The 12 SADC countries are Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. They represent 40 percent of the population of the African continent and more than 80 percent of Africa's GNP.
"SADC is seen as an emerging economic and political force in Africa with which the EU has established an important co-operative relationship," Spring said.
